question.prompt:
Daphne is visited periodically by her three best friends: Alice, Beatrix, and Claire. Alice visits every third day, Beatrix visits every fourth day, and Claire visits every fifth day.

All three friends visited Daphne yesterday. How many days of the next \(365\)-day period will exactly two friends visit her?

solutions.explanation:
Label yesterday day \(0\), so the period we count consists of days \(1\) through \(365\). Two friends visit together whenever the day number is a common multiple of their visiting intervals.

Alice and Beatrix visit together every \(\operatorname{lcm}(3,4)=12\) days, Alice and Claire every \(15\) days, and Beatrix and Claire every \(20\) days. Among days \(1\) through \(365\), these pairs visit together \(30\), \(24\), and \(18\) times, respectively. Thus there are
\[
30+24+18=72
\]
pair occurrences.

A day with exactly two visitors contributes once to this count. A day with all three visitors contributes three times, once for each pair, and must contribute nothing to our answer. All three visit together every \(\operatorname{lcm}(3,4,5)=60\) days, giving \(6\) such days in the period. Days with fewer than two visitors were never counted. Therefore the required number is
\[
72-3\cdot6=\boxed{54},
\]
which is choice \(\text{B}\).
solutions.title: Count pair visits and remove triples

solutions.explanation:
Label yesterday day \(0\). Because \(60\) is a multiple of \(3\), \(4\), and \(5\), all three visiting schedules repeat every \(60\) days.

Within days \(1\) through \(60\), the days with exactly two visitors are:

Alice and Beatrix only: \(12,24,36,48\).

Alice and Claire only: \(15,30,45\).

Beatrix and Claire only: \(20,40\).

These lists come from the multiples of \(12\), \(15\), and \(20\), with day \(60\) removed because all three friends visit then. Every day with exactly two visitors belongs to exactly one of the three lists, so the block contains \(4+3+2=9\) qualifying days.

Since
\[
365=6\cdot60+5,
\]
there are six complete blocks and five remaining days. Those remaining days have the same visiting pattern as days \(1\) through \(5\), when no two friends visit together. Thus the answer is
\[
6\cdot9=\boxed{54},
\]
choice \(\text{B}\).
solutions.title: Count one repeating block
